open_questions: Three Brothers: confirm payment policy (historically cash-only) and whether they take reservations for Sunday Oct 25 at 4:00 PM; call 414-481-7530.
Sanford: a 5:30 PM Friday/Saturday seating for the 4-course prix fixe is tight against a 7:30 PM show; call 414-276-9608 (Tue-Sat 1-9 PM) and tell them the hard stop.
Solly's Grille hours (Fri/Sat 7:00 AM-7:00 PM, closed Sun/Mon) come from a third-party listing, not the restaurant; confirm by phone 414-332-8808.
Milwaukee Brat House: bar is open until 2:00-2:30 AM but kitchen cutoff for brats/curds after the show is not published; call 414-273-8709.
Ian's Pizza Downtown: open until 2:00 AM Fri/Sat, but whether by-the-slice is sold all the way to close is not stated on the site.
Kopp's: flavor-of-the-day list is company-wide; confirm the Greenfield store carries the same flavors on Monday Oct 26.
Lakefront Brewery: fish fry reservations are limited to 4:00-4:30 PM and 6:00-6:30 PM slots; otherwise first come, first served at the host stand. Book the 4:00 PM slot Friday if possible.

destination.name: Lakefront Brewery Beer Hall - Friday Night Fish Fry
destination.blurb: Friday in Milwaukee means fish fry, and this is the one with a live polka band in a riverside beer hall. Beer-battered cod, potato pancakes, a Riverwest Stein, and the Brewhaus Polka Kings from 5 to 8 PM, ten minutes from the Riverside.
destination.why_special: Lakefront is the Friday fish fry out-of-towners remember: a cavernous former power plant on the Milwaukee River, table service with cocktails on Fridays only, and a weekly polka band. The whole Wisconsin ritual (fish, rye bread, slaw, polka, brandy) in one room, and the closest proper fish fry to the theater. Never been inside, but the fish fry has a polka band, and that is enough.
must_order: Fish Fry Dinner: three-piece beer-battered cod with potato pancakes and applesauce ($20)
Fried Walleye, hand-breaded, two pieces ($23)
Cheese curds from the Cheese Curd Flavor of the Month board
A Riverwest Stein or Fixed Gear on draft, plus a brandy Old Fashioned sweet

reservation.note: Limited reservations for the 4:00-4:30 PM and 6:00-6:30 PM slots only, otherwise first come, first served. Parties of 9+ call 414-372-8800.

destination.best_window: Friday Oct 23: arrive at 4:00 PM when the fish fry kitchen opens, polka at 5:00 PM, out by 6:30 PM for doors

hours_this_weekend.fri: 11:00 AM - 9:00 PM (fish fry kitchen 4:00 - 9:00 PM, table service)

destination.travel_from_downtown: 6 min rideshare (1.2 mi) or a 25 min walk north along the RiverWalk

destination.name: Three Brothers Serbian Restaurant
destination.address: 2414 S St Clair St, Milwaukee, WI 53207
destination.blurb: A 1956 Serbian family restaurant inside an old Schlitz tiled-corner tavern in Bay View, run by the founder's widow and daughters, and a James Beard America's Classic (2002). The burek is baked to order and takes about half an hour, so it goes in first.
destination.why_special: The menu has barely changed in 70 years, the dining room is a Schlitz tavern with vintage floral plates and dim lamps, and the food is a Serbian grandmother's Sunday table. It opens at 4:00 PM on Sunday, which fits an early dinner before the last show. I haven't eaten here. Every Milwaukee critic I read has, and they agree on the burek.
must_order: Burek (spinach and cheese, or meat), a giant baked phyllo pie, about 30 minutes to bake ($26.50)
Chicken paprikash with potato dumplings
Roast lamb with house-pickled cabbage
Serbian salad and a glass of Serbian wine or slivovitz

reservation.note: Call 414-481-7530. Small room, so call ahead for Sunday at 4:00 PM, and bring cash in case (historically cash-only).

destination.best_window: Sunday Oct 25 at 4:00 PM (opens 4:00 PM Sat/Sun), or Saturday at 4:00 PM
destination.travel_from_downtown: 12 min rideshare (4 mi south to Bay View)

destination.name: Sanford Restaurant
destination.blurb: Milwaukee's fine-dining standard since 1989, in the D'Amato family's former corner grocery. A quiet 20-table room, polished service, and a seasonal four-course prix fixe. One dressed-up dinner this weekend belongs here.
destination.why_special: Chef-owner Justin Aprahamian (James Beard Best Chef Midwest) runs the restaurant Sandy D'Amato made famous. It has been on every Milwaukee best-of list for 35 years and still feels like a secret because it seats so few people.
must_order: Four-course Prix Fixe ($105), the whole point
Surprise seven-course tasting menu ($135) only Tue-Fri, so Friday if time allows
Whatever the duck preparation is that night

reservation.note: Phone only: 414-276-9608, Tue-Sat 1:00-9:00 PM. First seating is 5:30 PM Fri / 5:00 PM Sat. Tell them about the 7:30 PM show.

destination.best_window: Saturday Oct 24 at 5:00 PM (first seating) is the safest fit. Friday's first seating is 5:30 PM
destination.travel_from_downtown: 6 min rideshare (1.3 mi) or 25 min walk

destination.name: Odd Duck
destination.blurb: Walker's Point's playful, globally minded small-plates room, a regular on Milwaukee Magazine's best-restaurants list. The menu changes constantly, the bar opens at 3:00 PM with a $7 spritz happy hour, and the kitchen fires at 5:00 PM, which is pre-show dinner timing.
destination.why_special: The shareable menu changes so often that no two visits match, the front of house is known for warmth, and the bar and patio seats are walk-in. Wander in at 4:30 PM, drink through happy hour, and eat at 5:00 PM without a booking.
must_order: Ask for the current duck preparation (there is always one)
Three or four shareable plates across the vegetable and seafood sections
Happy hour 3:00-6:00 PM at the bar: $7 spritz, $5 draft, $8 wine

reservation.note: Resy for dining-room tables. Bar, bar tables and patio are first come, first served. 3% credit card surcharge (debit exempt).

destination.best_window: Friday or Saturday: bar at 4:30 PM for happy hour, kitchen at 5:00 PM, out by 6:45 PM
destination.travel_from_downtown: 7 min rideshare (1.5 mi) or 30 min walk south through the Third Ward

destination.name: Birch
destination.blurb: Seasonal Midwestern cooking from a wood-fired hearth in a handsome room just north of downtown, with a 4:00-6:00 PM happy hour and a burger Milwaukee Magazine calls top-tier. Dinner starts at 5:00 PM Friday and Saturday.
destination.why_special: Chef Kyle Knall (James Beard semifinalist) cooks almost everything over an open hearth. It is the most New York-feeling room in the city while still being about Wisconsin farms. Milwaukee Magazine Best Restaurants 2025. This one is on reputation.
must_order: Anything from the hearth: the whole roasted fish or the wood-fired pork
The Birch burger (a Milwaukee Magazine top pick)
Happy hour 4:00-6:00 PM Friday at the bar before dinner
destination.best_window: Friday Oct 23: happy hour at 4:00 PM, then 5:00 PM dinner. Or Saturday at 5:00 PM
destination.travel_from_downtown: 5 min rideshare (1.1 mi) or 22 min walk up Water St

destination.name: Mader's Restaurant
destination.address: 1041 N Old World 3rd St, Milwaukee, WI 53203
destination.blurb: Milwaukee's 120-year-old German landmark on Old World Third Street: suits of armor, stained glass, a Hofbrau pour, and a pork shank that calls for a nap. Ten minutes on foot from the Riverside, and open Sunday and Monday when much of the city is dark.
destination.why_special: It is the surviving old-world German dining room of Beer City (Karl Ratzsch closed in 2017), it has fed presidents and rock stars, and it is the walkable backup for a Milwaukee-flavored meal any day of the trip, including a late Monday lunch before the flight.
must_order: Bavarian Platter (schnitzel, kassler, bratwurst, sauerkraut, spaetzle)
Wiener Schnitzel
Roasted pork shank
A brandy Old Fashioned sweet, the Wisconsin way, or a liter of Hofbrau

reservation.note: Resy. Walk-ins fine at off hours. 414-271-3377.

destination.best_window: Sunday Oct 25 early dinner at 4:30 PM, or Monday 11:30 AM lunch before the airport
destination.travel_from_downtown: 10 min walk (0.5 mi) from the Riverside

destination.name: Solly's Grille
destination.address: 4629 N Port Washington Rd, Glendale, WI 53212
destination.blurb: Home of the butter burger since 1936 and a James Beard America's Classic (2022): a horseshoe lunch counter where the patty is steamed in butter and then topped with a melting slab of more butter. A real malt goes with it. Lunch only, closed Sunday and Monday, so Friday or Saturday.
destination.why_special: The butter burger is Milwaukee's signature sandwich and Solly's is its birthplace. The Beard Foundation singled it out in 2022. One at the counter with the regulars is a lunch that exists nowhere else. I haven't had one, and I still respect a kitchen that butters the bun and then adds more butter.
must_order: The Original Butter Burger (ask for grilled onions)
A chocolate malt or shake
Fries
destination.best_window: Saturday Oct 24 late breakfast or lunch (opens 7:00 AM), or Friday lunch
destination.travel_from_downtown: 12 min rideshare (5.5 mi north via I-43)
destination.hours_note: Hours from a third-party listing; confirm by phone (see open_questions).

destination.name: La Dama
destination.blurb: Chef Emmanuel Corona's mural-walled Mexican kitchen in Walker's Point, the South Side's old Mexican heart. Mole poblano and mole negro from his childhood, a deep mezcal list, and a 4:30 PM Sunday opening that fits the early-dinner window exactly.
destination.why_special: Milwaukee Magazine Best Restaurants 2025 called it an inventive, elegant take on Mexican cuisine. It is the destination version of the South Side's Mexican tradition rather than a taqueria, and one of the few serious restaurants open for an early Sunday dinner.
must_order: Mole poblano or mole negro (the house signatures)
Octopus
A mezcal flight or a mezcal cocktail
Churros or the dessert of the night
destination.best_window: Sunday Oct 25 at 4:30 PM (the alternative to Three Brothers), or Fri/Sat at 5:00 PM

street_food.name: 3rd Street Market Hall
street_food.blurb: A food hall with twenty-plus stalls and a bar two blocks west of the Riverside, on the same side of Wisconsin Avenue. Lao food at SapSap, Cambodian sandwiches at Num Pang, Wisconsin cheese curds and mac at Rod-N-Makk, tacos at Kompali, Pizza Shuttle slices, Bebe Zito ice cream. Open until 10:00 PM Fri/Sat, so it is the pre-show grazing hall.
street_food.why_special: The closest food to the venue, with real range: SapSap (Lao, family recipes), Anytime Arepa, Mr. Dye's Pies, Kawa ramen. There is an on-site bar, a self-serve beer wall, and games.
must_order: SapSap: Lao sausage or khao poon
Rod-N-Makk: Wisconsin cheese curds and a mac bowl
Num Pang: Cambodian sandwich on house baguette
Mr. Dye's Pies: a slice for the walk to the show
street_food.best_window: Any day for lunch or a 5:00-6:30 PM pre-show bite. Sunday closes at 7:00 PM

hours_this_weekend.sat: Food hall 9:00 AM - 10:00 PM; bar 11:00 AM - 11:00 PM

street_food.name: Milwaukee Public Market
street_food.blurb: The Third Ward's market hall: St. Paul Fish Company's lobster rolls and oysters at the palapa bar, West Allis Cheese & Sausage's curds, C. Adam's cakes, Thief Wine's bar upstairs, Anodyne coffee. A ten-minute walk from the Riverside and the best late-breakfast-into-lunch stroll downtown.
street_food.why_special: Nineteen independent merchants and seven bars under one roof, and St. Paul Fish Co. alone is a reason to go (a Bloody Mary and a half-dozen oysters at the bar is a Milwaukee Saturday). The Third Ward's boutiques and the RiverWalk are right outside.
must_order: St. Paul Fish Company: lobster roll, chowder, or oysters at the palapa bar with a Bloody Mary
West Allis Cheese & Sausage Shoppe: fresh cheese curds and a Usinger-style sausage sampler
C. Adam's Bakery: a kringle slice or cake
Thief Wine: a glass on the mezzanine
street_food.best_window: Saturday Oct 24 late breakfast or lunch, 11:00 AM - 1:00 PM. Also Sunday until 6:00 PM
street_food.travel_from_downtown: 10 min walk (0.5 mi) east over the river and south on Water St

street_food.name: Real Chili (Downtown)
street_food.blurb: Milwaukee's post-bar ritual since 1931: a counter, a bowl of chili ladled over spaghetti and beans, mild to hot, a fistful of oyster crackers, and a dash of hot vinegar. Open until 3:00 AM Friday and Saturday, ten minutes' walk from the theater.
street_food.why_special: The Milwaukee late-night meal, a 95-year-old counter joint with its own vocabulary (Marquette special, with or without beans, mild/medium/hot). Nothing else downtown is this old, this cheap, or open this late. Never been. Chili over spaghetti at 1 AM does not need a second opinion.
must_order: Marquette Special: chili over spaghetti with beans, medium heat
Chili cheese dog
Oyster crackers and the hot vinegar shaker on the counter
A cold Miller High Life
street_food.best_window: Friday or Saturday after the show, 11:45 PM - 1:00 AM (the downtown location is closed Sunday)

hours_this_weekend.sun: Closed (Marquette location at 1625 W Wells open 11:00 AM - 10:00 PM)

street_food.travel_from_downtown: 10 min walk (0.5 mi) east across the Wisconsin Ave bridge, north on Milwaukee St to Wells

street_food.name: Ian's Pizza Downtown (Cream City Arcade)
street_food.blurb: Wisconsin's cult by-the-slice shop (born in Madison), with a downtown location that doubles as an arcade, open until 2:00 AM Friday and Saturday. The Mac n' Cheese slice is the thing. A 14-minute walk north of the Riverside, or a 4-minute ride.
street_food.why_special: Late-night Wisconsin pizza culture in one slice: mac and cheese on a crust. The arcade makes it a post-show hang rather than a snack stop.
must_order: Signature Mac n' Cheese slice
Whatever the rotating specialty slice is (often a Wisconsin-themed one)
Garlic butter and ranch on the side, the local way
street_food.best_window: Friday or Saturday after the show, before 2:00 AM. Sunday closes at 10:00 PM
street_food.travel_from_downtown: 14 min walk (0.7 mi) north on Water St, or 4 min rideshare

street_food.name: Milwaukee Brat House (Downtown)
street_food.address: 1013 N Old World 3rd St, Milwaukee, WI 53203
street_food.blurb: A beer-and-brats tavern on Old World Third, next door to Mader's and a 9-minute walk from the venue. Brats with kraut, fried cheese curds, pretzels, and a bar open until 2:00 AM every night including Sunday, which makes it the late-night Milwaukee cliche after the Sunday show.
street_food.why_special: A bratwurst with sauerkraut and a Wisconsin beer in a downtown tavern is the plain, correct Milwaukee snack, and this is the walkable one open after midnight on Sunday.
must_order: Classic bratwurst with sauerkraut and stadium mustard
Fried Wisconsin cheese curds
A local draft (Lakefront, New Glarus Spotted Cow if they have it)
street_food.best_window: Sunday Oct 25 after the show (bar to 2:00 AM, confirm kitchen hours), or any afternoon
street_food.travel_from_downtown: 9 min walk (0.45 mi) from the Riverside
street_food.hours_note: Bar hours; kitchen cutoff not published (see open_questions).

street_food.name: Pizza Shuttle
street_food.blurb: The East Side's 40-year late-night institution: takeout and delivery until 3:00 AM every night, including Sunday, with a dine-in room until midnight. Pizza, broasted chicken, gyros, wonton mozzarella sticks, and a strawberry custard shake. The Sunday-night safety net that delivers to a downtown hotel.
street_food.why_special: When Real Chili is closed (Sunday) and everything downtown has stopped serving, Pizza Shuttle is still frying broasted chicken at 2:00 AM and delivering to downtown addresses. On reputation, and the reputation is 40 years of 2 AM.
must_order: A slice or small pie (the Deluxe)
Broasted chicken
Wonton mozzarella sticks
Strawberry shake made with fresh custard
street_food.best_window: Sunday Oct 25 after the show: delivery to the hotel, or dine in before midnight

milwaukee_food_traditions.name: Friday fish fry
milwaukee_food_traditions.what: Wisconsin's Catholic-Lent-turned-every-Friday ritual: beer-battered or breaded cod (or lake perch, walleye, bluegill) with rye bread, coleslaw, potato pancakes or fries, tartar sauce, and a brandy Old Fashioned. Breweries, church halls, supper clubs and taverns all do one, and Lakefront adds a live polka band. The other two legends are Kegel's Inn in West Allis (Fridays 11:00 AM - 9:00 PM, lake perch and walleye, 1924 speakeasy) and American Serb Hall (Fridays 3:30 - 8:30 PM, famous Serbian-sauce cod), both a 15-minute ride.

milwaukee_food_traditions.name: Butter burger
milwaukee_food_traditions.what: A thin griddled patty on a bun that has been slathered (not brushed) with butter, so it pools into the beef. Solly's invented it in 1936, and Kopp's and Culver's spread it statewide. Fried onions and a malt go with it.

milwaukee_food_traditions.name: Frozen custard
milwaukee_food_traditions.what: Dense, egg-rich soft-serve kept warmer than ice cream, sold by the dish, cone or pint from drive-in stands with a chalkboard Flavor of the Day. Kopp's publishes the schedule: Mr. Baseball (caramel malt with beer nuts and a splash of Miller Lite) on Friday Oct 23, Wedding Cake and German Apple Streusel on Saturday, Mint Chip and Heavenly Hash on Sunday, Twix-Tac-Dough and Cookies 'N Cream on Monday Oct 26.

milwaukee_food_traditions.name: Cheese curds
milwaukee_food_traditions.what: Fresh, squeaky cheddar curds eaten raw (they squeak against your teeth when they are a day old) or beer-battered and deep-fried with ranch. Lakefront's CurdWagon is fully gluten-free and runs a Cheese Curd Flavor of the Month. West Allis Cheese & Sausage in the Public Market sells fresh ones by the bag.

milwaukee_food_traditions.name: Brandy Old Fashioned (sweet or sour, with press)
milwaukee_food_traditions.what: Wisconsin drinks more Korbel brandy than any other state, and the Old Fashioned here is brandy (not whiskey) muddled with sugar, bitters and an orange slice and cherry, then topped with a soda of choice: 'sweet' (7UP or Sprite), 'sour' (Squirt or sour mix), 'press' (half 7UP, half seltzer) or 'seltzer.' Order it as 'brandy old fashioned sweet' and watch the bartender nod. Mader's and any fish fry bar will make a proper one, and Lakefront serves cocktails at the Friday fish fry.

milwaukee_food_traditions.name: Bloody Mary with a beer chaser
milwaukee_food_traditions.what: In Wisconsin a Bloody Mary comes with a 'snit' or 'chaser,' a few ounces of beer in a short glass on the side, and the garnish often becomes a meal: cheese curds, sausage, pickles, a shrimp, sometimes a whole slider or a fried chicken. Sobelman's built a national reputation on its 'Bloody Masterpiece' and its bacon-wrapped cheddar balls on a skewer. St. Paul Fish Co. in the Public Market pours them with oysters, and Honeypie infuses its own.

monday_brunch_before_flight.name: Uncle Wolfie's Breakfast Tavern (Downtown)
monday_brunch_before_flight.blurb: Milwaukee's favorite breakfast tavern, now with a downtown room eight minutes' walk from the Riverside. Walk-in only, open 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM Monday, and the Monday crowd is a fraction of the weekend line.
monday_brunch_before_flight.why_special: The easiest great brunch on a Monday: no rideshare, open from 8:00 AM, and a kitchen (exec chef Kristen Schwab) good enough that the same room runs a Tock-reserved tasting-menu dinner called The Wolf Wednesday through Saturday nights.
must_order: The breakfast sandwich or any egg plate with the house potatoes
A Bloody Mary (it is a breakfast tavern) or the coffee cocktail
Whatever pastry is on the counter

reservation.note: Walk-in only for brunch at both locations.

monday_brunch_before_flight.best_window: Monday Oct 26, 9:30 - 11:00 AM: checkout, brunch, then a 15 min ride to MKE
monday_brunch_before_flight.travel_from_downtown: 8 min walk (0.4 mi) from the Riverside; 15 min rideshare to MKE from here

monday_brunch_before_flight.name: Honeypie Cafe
monday_brunch_before_flight.blurb: Bay View's Midwestern-comfort cafe with house-baked pies the critics line up for, buttermilk biscuits, and house-infused Bloody Marys. It sits on Kinnickinnic Avenue, on the way to the airport (10 minutes from MKE), and it is open Monday from 9:00 AM.
monday_brunch_before_flight.why_special: A slice of Wisconsin pie for the plane, biscuits and gravy, and a Bloody Mary with a snit, in the neighborhood halfway between downtown and the airport. Check bags, ride to Bay View, eat, ride 10 minutes to MKE. I have not had the pie. People who have talk about it the way people talk about a grandmother's.
must_order: A slice of pie (ask what came out of the oven; take a second slice to go)
Buttermilk biscuits and gravy
House-infused Bloody Mary with a beer chaser

reservation.note: First come, first served. No reservations.

monday_brunch_before_flight.best_window: Monday Oct 26, 10:00 - 11:30 AM, then 10 min to MKE for a 3:00 PM flight
monday_brunch_before_flight.travel_from_downtown: 10 min rideshare (3.5 mi) from the Riverside; 10 min from here to MKE

monday_brunch_before_flight.name: Sobelman's Pub & Grill (original, St. Paul Ave)
monday_brunch_before_flight.address: 1900 W St Paul Ave, Milwaukee, WI 53233
monday_brunch_before_flight.blurb: The 1890s Schlitz tavern in the Menomonee Valley that made Milwaukee's over-garnished Bloody Mary famous (bacon-wrapped cheddar balls, sausage, a beer chaser), backed by a top-tier burger. Opens 11:00 AM Monday, a late Monday brunch disguised as lunch, and I-94 to the airport is right there.
monday_brunch_before_flight.why_special: The Bloody Mary with a beer chaser is a Wisconsin tradition and Sobelman's turned it into a spectacle (the Bloody Masterpiece, the Baconado). The original tavern at 11:00 AM on a Monday with a Sobelman burger is the send-off meal. Closed Sunday, so Saturday (opens 10:00 AM) or Monday.
must_order: The Bloody Masterpiece (or the Baconado) with the beer chaser
The Sobelman burger (or the Beast)
Bacon-wrapped jalapeno cheeseballs
monday_brunch_before_flight.best_window: Monday Oct 26 at the 11:00 AM open, out by 12:15 PM, 15 min drive to MKE. Or Saturday at 10:00 AM
monday_brunch_before_flight.travel_from_downtown: 7 min rideshare (1.8 mi west); 15 min from here to MKE via I-94/I-43

monday_brunch_before_flight.name: Kopp's Frozen Custard (Greenfield, on the way to MKE)
monday_brunch_before_flight.blurb: Milwaukee's custard temple: a stainless-steel stand on Layton Avenue, the road that runs straight east to the airport. Two Flavors of the Day on a chalkboard and jumbo butter burgers. Monday Oct 26 flavors are Twix-Tac-Dough and Cookies 'N Cream.
monday_brunch_before_flight.why_special: Frozen custard is the dessert Milwaukee is proudest of and Kopp's is the name every local says first. Layton Avenue runs directly to MKE (about 12 minutes), so a dish of custard and a jumbo butter burger is the last Milwaukee stop before security.
must_order: A dish of the Flavor of the Day (Monday: Twix-Tac-Dough or Cookies 'N Cream)
Jumbo butter burger with fried onions
Caramel Apple Sundae (October sundae of the month)
monday_brunch_before_flight.best_window: Monday Oct 26, 11:30 AM - 12:30 PM, then 12 min east on Layton Ave to MKE
monday_brunch_before_flight.travel_from_downtown: 18 min rideshare (10 mi) from downtown; 12 min from here to MKE
